priceNote: Self-fetched today (live-prices.json cache dated Aug 13, too stale to use). Up modestly from $9.65 (Aug 5) but the pattern flagged last report has repeated and intensified: three separate commercial-win announcements in September each produced a same-day decline (LUMI -1.63%, Toyo -5.09%, Brazil -4.93%) — good news is still not being rewarded.
summary: IQM's commercial momentum has genuinely accelerated since the last report — a second full-stack system sale to Toyo (Japan, Sep 15), a first South American deployment via Brazil's Eldorado Research Institute (Sep 17), and a staged upgrade path selected by Finland's LUMI AI Factory toward logical qubits (Sep 10) — plus BTIG initiated coverage at Buy with a $20 target (~Sep 21), the first fresh sell-side validation since the IPO. Yet the stock fell on EVERY one of those three announcement days (-1.63%, -5.09%, -4.93%), the exact 'good news doesn't move this stock' pattern the last report flagged, now with three more data points confirming it's persistent rather than a one-off. Analyst coverage remains thin (2 analysts: BTIG Buy $20, Redburn Hold $12.88, average $16.44) — per this run's tier2 feedback, IQMX's catalystType (partnership_win) is a measured LAGGARD across the turbo lane (medianExcessVsBenchPct -3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16), which argues for keeping conviction and sizing small even as the underlying commercial story improves. Cash (€309.4M, runway into Q2 2028) removes survival risk.
